status: Secondary hypothesis formulated during the audit, after earlier model comparisons. No independent source or preregistration. This protocol was fixed before calculating the popularity comparison on the five-city transfer cohort.
hypothesis: On the five-city transfer cohort, conditioning on the last observed attraction improves user- and city-macro NDCG@5 relative to the same city's training popularity.
cohort: Reuse all 81 disjoint-user contexts from the frozen transfer test. Exclude the last attraction for both methods; preserve all other candidates. No retuning.
inference: Paired global-user bootstrap, 10000 draws, and two-sided sign permutations with the same weights/signs in each city; report sensitivity by city, leave one city out, and pooled user macro. This test is exploratory and not part of H1/H2 Holm family.
support: Positive delta and 95% interval entirely above zero, with two-sided p < .05; otherwise not supported.
comparator: Popularity = frequency of cultural visits in training sequences, with the same final exclusion of the last place and deterministic tie handling.
